title: Marine Chain: North Korea's fake crypto fleet

scenes.narration: [serious] Officials say North Korean hackers secretly ran a shipping business online.
It was called Marine Chain. In 2017 and 2018, it sold digital shares of real cargo ships.
The idea: buy a small piece of a ship. It even tried to sell on a market in Hong Kong.

items: Own a piece of a ship

scenes.narration: But America says North Korea secretly controlled it. The goal was to get money around American bans.
In February 2021, America charged three army hackers, including Park Jin Hyok.
Officials tied them to plans to steal over 1.3 billion dollars. The ships, they say, were a cover.

facts.claim: Per the indictment, the Marine Chain Platform was developed and marketed in 2017 and 2018, with a Marine Chain Token and Initial Coin Offering, offering fractional ownership of marine shipping vessels via blockchain
The indictment alleges the scheme would let North Korea secretly obtain funds from investors, control vessel interests and evade U.S. sanctions
The hackers sought approval from Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission to trade the token as a security
Jon Chang Hyok (31), Kim Il (27) and Park Jin Hyok (36), of North Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau, were charged; indictment dated Dec 8, 2020, unsealed Feb 17, 2021
DOJ says the defendants conspired to steal and extort more than $1.3 billion of money and cryptocurrency
